messages:
lee: Hi all, new hire here. I copied the kubeconfigs from the onboarding email into ~/.kube/redwood and set KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood:~/.kube/config but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows only my local minikube context. The staging context isn't showing up.

onboarding-bot: Welcome @lee! The onboarding bundle should include a file named `redwood-staging.yaml` with contexts. Did you download the tarball and extract? Link: https://internal.redwood/onboard/lee-assets

lee: I extracted the tar and I can see a file `redwood-staging.yaml` with clusters/users/contexts sections. When I run `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood config view` it prints clusters and users, but `contexts:` is missing from the output.

carl: That usually means one of the kubeconfig files has an unexpected top-level field that prevents merging. Can you paste the top of `~/.kube/redwood` (first 20 lines) here (sanitize tokens)?

lee: pasted: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
preferences: {}
clusters:
- cluster:
    server: https://staging-api.us-west1.redwood.internal
    certificate-authority-data: <redacted>
  name: staging-cluster
users:
- name: lee@redwood
  user:
    token: <redacted>
```
(no contexts block)

tal: That's the issue: the onboarding generator forgot to write contexts in that kubeconfig; some tools rely on contexts to select cluster+user. Two quick fixes: 1) create a context locally with `kubectl config set-context` (recommended), or 2) use `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood --cluster=staging-cluster --user=lee@redwood` with direct flags (less ergonomic).

carl: To create the context: 
```
kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood config set-context staging-us-west1 --cluster=staging-cluster --user=lee@redwood
kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood config use-context staging-us-west1
kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood get ns
```
That will persist the context in the file.

lee: I ran that and `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood get pods -n staging` errors with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. My browser can hit the API HTTPS endpoint fine.

onboarding-bot: Onboarding note: if you see cert errors, check for `certificate-authority-data` vs `certificate-authority` fields. If CA is provided as a file path but not present on your machine, kubectl will fail.

carl: Run `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood config view --raw | yq e '.clusters[].cluster' -` to inspect cluster definitions. If CA is missing, I can re-issue an onboarding bundle with `certificate-authority-data` embedded.

lee: Output shows `certificate-authority: /etc/redwood/ca.pem` (which doesn't exist locally).

infra-bot: Ticket created: ONBOARD-9217. Action: regenerate kubeconfig for lee with embedded CA data. ETA 30m.

carl: Temporary workaround: if you trust the cluster and are on a trusted network, you can `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/redwood --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true get pods -n staging` but don't do that for long. I'll wait for infra to push the fixed config.

lee: Thanks, tried the insecure flag and I can list pods. Appreciate the fast triage.

tal: After infra updates the file we'll merge it into your `~/.kube/config` using `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` so you don't need KUBECONFIG env juggling. We'll also add a short note in the onboarding guide: "Always verify contexts and CA presence after extracting kubeconfigs."

lee: Sounds good. One more: who do I ping for namespace access if I need `edit` on `staging/dev` for a short task?

carl: File a request in #eng-infra with reason + duration and tag me or @tal. For view-level access we handle in-thread; edit requires approval.

lee: Great, closing the loop. Will wait for the regenerated file and will update the onboarding checklist entry if anything else pops up. Thanks! :smile:
